questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot 2x=\frac{2}{x}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x & =5\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =5\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})|+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{9\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =9\int \sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =9\int \sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =9\int {u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =9\cdot \frac{2{u}^{3/2}}{3}+C \\  & =6{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{{ln}^{3}⁡(3x)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{5}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{x{log}_{5}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{log}_{5}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{5}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{5}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {log}_{5}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5\cdot \frac{{log}_{5}^{2}⁡x}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{4}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =2\int {log}_{4}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot {u}^{2}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot {log}_{4}^{2}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{5}⁡({x}^{3}).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{3})}{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int {log}_{5}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int u\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{6}\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{6}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5{log}_{5}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})}{12}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{2}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x{log}_{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{log}_{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{2}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x).$ Then  we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{5x}\cdot 5=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e/5$ | ${e}^{4}/5$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e/5}^{{e}^{4}/5}\frac{3}{x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{e/5}^{{e}^{4}/5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =3{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3{\int }_{1}^{4}{u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot {\frac{{u}^{1/2}}{1/2}|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =6\cdot {\sqrt{u}|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =6(\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{1}) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})}{5x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{4}{5}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}u\cdot \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4}{15}{\int }_{0}^{3}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4}{15}\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{15}\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{8}⁡(2x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\cdot 2=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡8\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1/3$ | $2/3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{6{log}_{8}⁡(2x)}{x}\,\text{d}x & =6{\int }_{1}^{2}{log}_{8}⁡(2x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =6{\int }_{1/3}^{2/3}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡8\,\text{d}u \\  & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡8{\int }_{1/3}^{2/3}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡8\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{1/3}^{2/3} \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡8\cdot (\frac{4}{9}-\frac{1}{9}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡8\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{2}^{8}\frac{{log}_{2}⁡(2x)}{x}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡2$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{2}⁡(2x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot 2=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $2$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{8}\frac{{log}_{2}⁡(2x)}{x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{8}{log}_{2}⁡(2x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2{\int }_{2}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡2(16-4) \\  & =(6)\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | ${e}^{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {{u}^{2}|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({2}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's set $u = \ln x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= \dfrac 1 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\dfrac 1 x\,{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\int {u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot 2{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{u}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{\log^2_3 x }{x} \,\textrm d x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as

$$
\int \dfrac{(\log_3 x)^2 }{x} \,\textrm d x.
$$

Let $u=\log_3 x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = \dfrac{1}{x\ln 3}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ln 3\,\textrm d u = \dfrac 1 x \textrm d x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {u}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\int {u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{1}{3}{u}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3({log}_{3}⁡x)^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3{log}_{3}^{3}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u = \ln x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= \dfrac 1 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\dfrac 1 x\,{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | $e^2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
	\int_{e}^{e^2} \dfrac{\ln^2 x}{x}\,\textrm{d}x
&= \int_{e}^{e^2} (\ln x)^2\cdot \dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{x}\[5pt]
&=\int_{1}^{2} u^2\,\textrm{d}u\[5pt]
&=\left.\dfrac13u^{3}\right|_{1}^{2}\[5pt] 
&=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2^3-1^3 \right)\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(8-1 \right)\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{7}{3}		

	}
$$
